reason: §1150 lists circumcision among the Old Covenant liturgical signs and says 'The Church sees in these signs a prefiguring of the sacraments of the New Covenant'. That is explicit wording, and the antitype is rightly the sacraments in general, since §1150 does not pair any sign with one sacrament.

'Laying on of hands' is named in the same §1150 list that the Church sees as 'a prefiguring of the sacraments of the New Covenant'. Explicit and Sacramental, and the general antitype matches the text.
'Sacrifices' stands in the §1150 list governed by 'The Church sees in these signs a prefiguring'. The explicit wording carries the link at the stated precision.
§1150 names 'above all the Passover' among the signs the Church sees as a prefiguring of the New Covenant sacraments. Explicit, and correctly general on the antitype side.
'He himself is the meaning of all these signs', said above all of the Passover, is fulfillment language with Christ as the stated term. Preparatory is right because there is no figure wording.
The same sentence says Christ gives new meaning 'above all to the Exodus' and 'is the meaning of all these signs'. That is a statement of fulfillment in Christ, so preparatory and Christological.
§1152 directly teaches about the sacraments ('they fulfill the types and figures of the Old Covenant'). A teaches row is right because it names no particular OT figure.

'Christ is the true temple of God, "the place where his glory dwells"' (Ps 26:8, language for the sanctuary) is a typological title that implies the Temple as its first term. With no figure wording, preparatory is the most it can be, and that is the label given.

§1217 opens the Vigil blessing's list as 'the great events in salvation history that already prefigured the mystery of Baptism:', and §1218 is the first item in it ('At the very dawn of creation your Spirit breathed on the waters'). 'Prefigured' governs this event directly, as it does for the flood and Red Sea rows labeled explicit, so the label should be explicit, not synthesized.
§1217 teaches about Baptism through the Easter Vigil blessing of the water. Correct as a teaches row.
'The Church has seen in Noah's ark a prefiguring of salvation by Baptism', citing 1 Pet 3:20, is plainly explicit. The Type, antitype and category are all correct.

The prayer in §1219 makes the flood waters 'a sign of the waters of Baptism', and the flood falls under §1217's 'events... that already prefigured the mystery of Baptism', so explicit holds. The flood (waters that end sin) is properly a separate Type from the ark (the vessel of salvation).
§1221 says the crossing 'announces the liberation wrought by Baptism', and the prayer calls it 'an image of the people set free in Baptism'. 'Image' makes it explicit, and an event-level Type fits.
'Baptism is prefigured in the crossing of the Jordan River' is explicit wording. The event-level Type and Sacramental category are correct.
§1222 calls 'the land promised to Abraham's descendants' 'an image of eternal life'. The image is the land, not the crossing, so the-promised-land is the right precision, and Eschatological is right.
§1223 teaches about Christ ('All the Old Covenant prefigurations find their fulfillment in Christ Jesus') without singling out one figure, so a teaches row is right.

§1224 draws the parallel itself: 'The Spirit who had hovered over the waters of the first creation descended then on the Christ as a prelude of the new creation', under §1223's 'All the Old Covenant prefigurations find their fulfillment in Christ Jesus'. There is no figure wording, so preparatory is right. The antitype is properly the event of Jesus' baptism, and Christological is right.

§1288 traces Confirmation's imposition of hands to the apostles and to Pentecost, not to any Old Testament gesture, and §1150 links the OT gesture only to the sacraments in general, so the Confirmation-specific pairing is not in the text. If a specific sacrament is wanted, §1538 (the laying on of hands as 'the visible sign of this ordination') with §1541 would support a tighter Holy Orders synthesis.

§1150's 'anointing and consecration of kings and priests' and §1294's 'anointing with sacred chrism in... ordination is the sign of consecration' share the sign, its meaning and the office, and §1541 confirms the line from OT priesthood to ordained ministry. Synthesized is right; strictly, the priests' anointing (Exod 29:7) is what is in view.

§1294 makes chrism in Confirmation 'the sign of consecration', which matches §1150's 'anointing and consecration', and §1289 grounds it in the name Christian, meaning 'anointed'. Taken together the paragraphs make the link plain, so synthesized and Sacramental hold.
Saying the Mass 'completes and surpasses all the sacrifices of the Old Covenant' is fulfillment language. Preparatory, Eucharist and Sacramental are all correct.

'The Church sees in the gesture of the king-priest Melchizedek, who "brought out bread and wine," a prefiguring of her own offering' is explicit. Strictly, the text's type is the gesture rather than the person, but the melchizedek Type's description already names the offering, so no split is needed.
The Passover bread and 'cup of blessing' receive from Jesus 'a new and definitive meaning' when he institutes the Eucharist. That is fulfillment language without figure wording, so preparatory fits.

'Jesus' passing over to his father by his death and Resurrection, the new Passover' is a typological title, together with 'gave the Jewish Passover its definitive meaning', so preparatory is right. The text's antitype is the whole Paschal passage (death and Resurrection); christs-passion is the closest existing Type but is narrower than the text.
'The Eucharist, which fulfills the Jewish Passover' is direct fulfillment wording. Preparatory and Sacramental are right.

The Offertory 'takes up the gesture of Melchizedek' and commits the gifts to Christ, who 'brings to perfection all human attempts to offer sacrifices'. That is fulfillment wording, not figure wording, so preparatory is right, and the row supports the explicit §1333 row.

Christ 'directed his disciples' attention toward the fulfillment of the Passover in the kingdom of God' (Lk 22:16-18). The type is the Passover as an institution, not a prophecy, fulfilled in the final kingdom, so preparatory and Eschatological are correct, and heaven is the nearest Type.
§1539 describes how the tribe of Levi was chosen and the priesthood of the Old Covenant consecrated. Correct teaches row.
§1540 teaches the purpose and limits of the OT priesthood (cf. Heb 7:11; 10:11). Correct teaches row; it speaks of an institution's insufficiency, not of a people.

'The liturgy of the Church... sees in... the institution of the seventy elders, a prefiguring of the ordained ministry of the New Covenant' is explicit. 'Ordained ministry' maps to holy-orders, and Sacramental is right.

The same sentence names 'the priesthood of Aaron and the service of the Levites' as a prefiguring of the ordained ministry. ot-priesthood (the institution, not Aaron the person) is the right precision.

The prayer for ordaining priests recalls Num 11:25 ('you extended the spirit of Moses to seventy wise men'), so a teaches row is right. The prayer places the elders as helpers 'next to [the high priests] in rank', which points to the presbyterate specifically.
'You shared among the sons of Aaron the fullness of their father's power' recalls the Aaronic priesthood. Correct teaches row.
The prayer for ordaining deacons recalls the sons of Levi as 'ministers of your tabernacle'. Correct teaches row for ot-priesthood (Levitical service).

Gen 1:2 is a distinct, concrete event: §1218 lists it among the events that 'prefigured' Baptism, and §1224 sets it beside the Spirit's descent at the Jordan. No existing water Type (gods-wonders-by-water, noahs-flood) covers creation, so a new Type is warranted.

Confirmation is a real sacrament that the NT column lacks, and it is distinct from Baptism and Holy Orders. The §1150 + §1294 anointing row survives verification (I reject the §1288 laying-on-of-hands row), so the Type has support.

§1150 names 'laying on of hands' among the Old Covenant signs that prefigure the sacraments, and no existing Type covers it. The description could also cite Num 8:10 (Israel lays hands on the Levites) and Lev 1:4 (hands on the offering), the liturgical uses closest to §1150's sense.
§1541 names 'the institution of the seventy elders' explicitly and §1542 recalls it. The description (Num 11:16-17, 24-25) is precise and properly distinct from ot-priesthood.
'Fulfilled by the beloved Son' refers to the Father's work in general; no OT figure is named.
Concerns liturgical song and music as signs; no typological content.
Contrasts the earlier impossibility of picturing God with the new 'economy of images' after the Incarnation; a doctrinal contrast, not a type and antitype.
'Like the figure of the precious and life-giving cross' (Nicaea II) uses 'figure' for a visual depiction, and 'in the image of God' concerns the nature of man; no OT type is linked to an NT antitype.

'Year of the Lord's favor' (Isa 61:2; Lk 4:19) is a prophetic phrase applied to the liturgical year, and 'fulfillment in the Passover of Jesus' refers to the economy of salvation in general. That is prophecy, not typology.
Describes the bishop's chair and the ambo; no typological content.
Cultures are 'redeemed and fulfilled' by Christ; this is about inculturation, not an OT type.
'Announces' links the Roman post-baptismal anointing to a later Confirmation, which are both Christian rites; no OT figure is involved.
